description: Word-match dot plot between two sequences, on both strands, returned as diagonal RUNS rather than points. This is the view that shows what a single best alignment hides: internal repeats, tandem duplications, and inversions — an inversion appears as a run on the falling diagonal and as nothing at all in a normal pairwise alignment. Compare a sequence with itself to map its own repeats. Word size is chosen from the input lengths when you do not set one, because too short a word fills the plot with chance matches that the eye reads as homology.

a.description: First sequence (raw or FASTA). Max 200,000 nt.

b.description: Second sequence. Pass the same sequence as "a" to find its internal repeats. Max 200,000 nt.

bothStrands.description: Also search the reverse complement, which is what reveals inversions.

maxRuns.description: Most runs to return, longest first.

minRunLength.description: Drop runs shorter than this before returning. 0 = keep every run at least wordSize long.

wordSize.description: Exact-match word length. Omit to pick one from the sequence lengths.

name: dot_plot
title: Dot plot (sequence comparison)
